title: My Go-To Creamy White Chicken Chili (The One-Pot 30-Minute Shortcut)
description: This creamy white chicken chili is the ultimate rainy day hug. It’s thick, rich, and tastes like it simmered for hours, but only takes one pot and 30 minutes.
story: It’s pouring outside my little apartment window today, the kind of gray Tuesday that just begs for a thick sweater and a bowl of something warm. I used to think white chicken chili needed eight hours in a crockpot to get that deep flavor, but I was so wrong. Last week, I actually tried to rush it on high heat and ended up scorching the bottom of my pot—total disaster. This version is my 'lesson learned' recipe. Using a rotisserie chicken from the store is my absolute favorite shortcut when I’m tired but still want that home-cooked feeling. I’ve got my favorite indie-folk playlist going, a knob of Kerrygold butter melting in the pot, and the smell of green chiles filling the kitchen. It’s pure comfort without the wait. Honestly, it is better than the slow cooker version because the chicken stays juicy instead of getting stringy. Just grab some tortilla chips and you are all set for the night.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans Aldi Dakota's Pride Great Northern beans, drained and rinsed
1 (4 oz) can Ortega chopped mild green chiles
1 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp dried oregano
4 oz cream cheese, softened and cubed
instructions: Step 1: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat. Sauté the onions until they are soft and see-through, then stir in the garlic for just a minute until the aroma fills your kitchen. Don't let the garlic brown or it'll taste bitter!
Step 2: Add the green chiles, cumin, and oregano. Let those spices toast in the warm butter for about 30 seconds—it really wakes up the flavor profile and smells incredible.

Step 3: Pour in the beans, chicken, and broth. Bring it to a gentle simmer. Take a potato masher and crush just a handful of the beans right in the pot; this makes the broth naturally thick and hearty.

Step 4: Turn the heat to low and stir in the cream cheese cubes. Keep stirring gently until they melt completely and the chili looks silky and rich. Add a pinch of kosher salt and black pepper to finish.
proHack: To get that 'simmered all day' thickness without the wait, mash about 1/2 cup of the white beans against the side of the pot before adding the cream cheese. It creates a natural starch base that makes the texture incredibly velvety.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. When reheating on the stove, add a splash of milk or extra broth because it thickens up a lot once it is cold. I don't recommend freezing this one because the cream cheese can get a bit grainy when it thaws.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the Great Northern beans?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Cannellini beans or even Navy beans from your pantry work perfectly here.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the cream cheese from curdling?
faqs.answer: Make sure your cream cheese is at room temperature before adding it, and keep the heat on low. Don't let the chili reach a rolling boil once the dairy is in there.
